newsitem.title: USA: Charleston, S.C., rejects $85 mln revenue bonds.
newsitem.headline: Charleston, S.C., rejects $85 mln revenue bonds.

text.p: South Carolina's Charleston City Council narrowly voted down a controversial $85 million bond issue to renovate a hospital for doctors affiliated with the Medical University of South Carolina.
The proposal was rejected in a 4-3 vote on Tuesday night, county officials said.
University Medical Associates, a nonprofit group of physicians affiliated with the university, had sought tax-exempt revenue bonds to renovate the building that formerly housed St. Francis Hospital.
The conduit financing proposal failed after private practice physicians said it would give an unfair advantage to the university doctors, who they compete against.

Council members rejected the plan earlier this year, then revived it, then rejected it again on Tuesday. The bond issue could be brought up again before the council, but only by one of the council members who opposed it this time.
